title: Exercise Northstar: D-7
description: One week out. The command screen crashes at 500 users. The exercise has 3,000.
storyContext: One week out. The [[stress test]] says the screen dies at 500 users. The exercise has 3,000. Your lead slides the report over: "The generals demo it Thursday. Fix it, or explain a blank screen to a two-star."

callbacks.arc1-ch2:cache-layer: That caching trick from rehearsal night is page one of your team playbook now. Time to write page two.

software-engineer.title: Fix the Overload
software-engineer.instruction: 3,000 users, each demanding a private data stream. The system chokes at 500. Fix it in 7 days.
software-engineer.hint: Share the resource smarter, or add more of it. Which fits 7 days?

options.label: Group users — 50 share one data stream instead of one each. Cuts load 95%, adds a 1-second delay.
options.consequence: Load collapses by 95%. Nobody notices the one-second delay. The budget officer notices the savings.

options.label: Add more identical machines and spread users evenly. Costs more; needs zero code changes.
options.consequence: More machines, zero drama. The invoice makes finance whimper, but Thursday's demo purrs.

options.label: Rewrite the connection system so one machine handles thousands. Could hit 10,000 users — big rewrite, 7 days left.
options.consequence: You bet everything on a rewrite... and it works Wednesday midnight. Legendary or reckless — nobody's sure.

options.label: Generals get live updates, officers 10-second delays, everyone else 30-second snapshots. Under 200 live connections.
options.consequence: Under 200 live connections. Generals get real-time; somewhere a corporal mutters about his 30-second snapshots.

data-scientist.title: Estimate Peak Users
data-scientist.instruction: Not all 3,000 log in at once. The graph shows peak simultaneous users (in hundreds) from past exercises. Estimate this one's peak.
data-scientist.hint: Is the growth steady or accelerating? Extend the pattern.
data-scientist.consequenceSuccess: Your estimate lands in range. Capacity gets sized just right — no crash, no waste.
data-scientist.consequenceFail: Peak users blow past your guess and the screen wobbles. Growth curves strike again.

cloud-engineer.title: Run the Stress Test
cloud-engineer.instruction: Before fixing anything, find every breaking point. Order the test steps.
cloud-engineer.hint: Record normal first. Then push until it breaks.

items.label: Record normal performance with 100 fake users
Climb to 500 users — note where things slow
Check machine load and memory at the break
Apply the fix, then run it all again

cloud-engineer.consequenceSuccess: You find the exact bolt that snaps at user 517. The fix team knows precisely what to fix.
cloud-engineer.consequenceFail: You push to the crash without a baseline — now you can't tell broken from normal. Restart the test.
